- If sentiment is positive (≥ 0.2) in recent days, model tends to underreact — increase forecast slightly to align with bullish momentum.  
- If sentiment is negative (≤ -0.2) in recent days, model tends to overreact — reduce forecast slightly to avoid bearish overcorrection.  
- Model consistently underestimates true price spikes in early 30d horizon — adjust forecast upward by 1–3% for spikes > 5% from prior 18d mean.  
- Model shows persistent lag in capturing true price reversals — add 1–2 day buffer for mean reversion events after sharp moves.  
- For 30d forecasts, if true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., > 10% drop from peak), model often overshoots downward — cap forecast decline at 5% below prior peak.  
- When sentiment is neutral (0.0) and history shows volatility, model tends to smooth too much — introduce 1–2% volatility buffer in forecast.  
- If true outcome deviates > 5% from 18d moving average, model often fails to adjust — force correction to align with 18d MA ± 2% unless sentiment overrides.
